## Purpose

This SOP describes procedures for collecting representative
groundwater samples from monitoring wells using the low-flow (minimal
drawdown) purging and sampling method. Low-flow sampling minimizes
disturbance to the well and surrounding formation, reduces turbidity
artifacts, and yields samples that are more representative of in-situ
groundwater chemistry than traditional high-volume purge methods
[@puls_barcelona1996].

The procedures follow EPA low-flow guidance [@puls_barcelona1996], EPA
Region 4 groundwater sampling procedures [@usepa_sesd301], and
Cal-EPA DTSC guidance on representative groundwater sampling.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Sampling of existing groundwater monitoring wells
  with an inside diameter of 2 inches (5 cm) or greater, screened
  intervals of 3 m (10 ft) or less, and a water level above the top
  of the screen
- **Does not apply to:** Well installation or development; direct-push
  (e.g., Geoprobe) sampling; spring or seep sampling; wells requiring
  high-volume purging for regulatory compliance; wells with water
  levels below the top of the screen (consult the PI for alternative
  procedures)
- **Location:** All EA Program groundwater monitoring sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Project Lead | Approve sampling plan and well selection                |
| Field Lead        | Coordinate logistics, maintain well access agreements   |
| Trained Personnel | Purge and sample wells per this SOP                     |
| New Students      | Complete training before participating in well sampling |


## Definitions

- **Dedicated pump:** A pump permanently installed in a single well and
  not removed between sampling events; eliminates inter-well
  cross-contamination and decontamination burden; preferred for long-
  term monitoring programs.
- **Drawdown:** The decline in water level within a well caused by
  pumping; in low-flow sampling, drawdown must remain at or below
  10 cm to minimize vertical mixing within the screened interval and
  preserve the representativeness of the sample [@puls_barcelona1996].
- **E-tape (electric tape, water level indicator):** An electronic
  device consisting of a two-conductor cable with a sensing probe at
  the tip; when the probe contacts the water surface, an audible alarm
  sounds; used to measure depth to water from a reference point
  (typically the top of casing, TOC).
- **Flow-through cell:** A sealed flow cell into which purge water is
  routed so that a multiparameter probe can measure field parameters
  continuously without exposure to the atmosphere; prevents degassing
  of CO~2~ and O~2~ that would bias pH, DO, and ORP readings.
- **High-volume purge:** The traditional well purging approach in which
  3--5 well volumes (or more) are removed before sampling; causes high
  drawdown, turbulence, and resuspension of fine particles; generally
  produces less representative samples than low-flow methods
  [@puls_barcelona1996].
- **Low-flow (minimal-drawdown) sampling:** A groundwater sampling
  technique in which the pump is set at the mid-screen interval and
  the flow rate is adjusted to maintain drawdown of 10 cm or less;
  sampling begins only after field parameters have stabilized
  [@puls_barcelona1996; @astm_d6771].
- **ORP (oxidation-reduction potential):** A measure of the
  electron-donating or -accepting capacity of a groundwater sample;
  expressed in millivolts; sensitive to exposure to atmospheric
  oxygen; must be measured in a flow-through cell without headspace.
- **Parameter stabilization:** The criterion indicating that the water
  being pumped from the well is representative of the aquifer rather
  than stagnant casing water; defined as three consecutive readings
  within specified limits for pH, temperature, specific conductance,
  DO, ORP, and turbidity (see §7.3 criteria table).
- **Screen interval (screened interval):** The perforated section of
  the well casing through which groundwater enters the well from the
  surrounding aquifer; the pump intake should be positioned at the
  center of this interval during low-flow sampling.
- **Standing water volume:** The volume of water within the well casing
  above the bottom of the well screen; calculated as
  $V = \pi r^2 h$, where $r$ is the inside casing radius and $h$ is
  the height of the water column; used to determine whether enough
  water exists for low-flow sampling.
- **TOC (top of casing):** The surveyed reference elevation from which
  all depth-to-water measurements are taken; must be marked on the
  well casing with a permanent reference point.
- **Trip blank:** A set of 40 mL VOC sample vials filled with
  laboratory-grade water in the lab, transported to the field in a
  sealed cooler alongside field samples, and returned to the lab
  unopened; detects contamination introduced during transport
  [@apha2012].
- **Well volume:** The volume of water stored in the well casing
  above the screen; typically calculated from well construction
  records; one well volume is the minimum purge volume before
  parameter monitoring in high-volume purge methods.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Heavy well caps and locks; lifting pumps and
  equipment; uneven terrain around well pads; potential for back
  strain when bending over flush-mount wells
- **Chemical:** Groundwater may contain VOCs, metals, or other
  contaminants. Purge water may require containerization as hazardous
  waste. Preservative acids in pre-preserved bottles are corrosive.
- **Biological:** Standing water in well vaults may harbor mosquitoes
  or other vectors
- **Confined spaces:** Flush-mount well vaults may be classified as
  confined spaces. Do not enter vaults.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (double-glove when handling suspected hazardous
      groundwater)
- [ ] Safety glasses or chemical splash goggles
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or field boots

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) and
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](../lab_sops/SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).


## Equipment and Materials

### Sampling Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Low-flow peristaltic pump or bladder pump | Programmable flow rate; 0.1--0.5 L/min |
| Pump tubing (dedicated or new)        | PTFE or polyethylene; appropriate ID for pump |
| Flow-through cell                     | With ports for multiparameter probe      |
| Multiparameter probe                  | pH, temperature, SpC, DO, ORP, turbidity; calibrated per instrument SOP |
| E-tape (water level indicator)        | Metric and/or English gradations         |
| Pre-labeled sample bottles            | Per analyte; type and preservative per project QA plan [@apha2012] |
| Deionized water                       | For equipment blanks and rinsing         |
| Well keys                             | For locked well caps                     |

### Field Documentation

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Well construction logs                | Casing depth, screen interval, diameter  |
| Groundwater purge log (Appendix A)    | For recording stabilization parameters   |
| Chain of custody (COC) forms          | Required for lab submission              |
| Field notebook                        |                                          |
| Camera                                | Photo-document well condition            |
| GPS unit or smartphone                | For confirming well locations            |


## Procedure

### Pre-Sampling Preparation

1. Review well construction logs for each well: casing material,
   diameter, total depth, screen interval, and previous water level
   data.
2. Calculate the volume of standing water in the well casing above
   the screen using $V = \pi r^2 h$.
3. Calibrate the multiparameter probe per the manufacturer's
   instructions. Record calibration data on the purge log.
4. Assemble pump, tubing, and flow-through cell. For non-dedicated
   equipment, decontaminate with deionized water before use at each
   well.

### Water Level Measurement

1. Remove the well cap. Note the condition of the well (damage,
   standing water in vault, obstructions).
2. Wipe the e-tape sensor with a clean paper towel.
3. Lower the e-tape slowly until the alarm sounds at the water surface.
4. Record depth to water from the TOC to the nearest 0.3 cm (0.01 ft).
5. Measure well depth from the same reference point (after sampling, to
   avoid resuspending settled solids).
6. Calculate the water column height and standing water volume.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Always measure water level before inserting the pump. Lowering the
pump displaces water and changes the apparent water level.
:::

### Pump Placement and Low-Flow Purging

1. Slowly lower the pump intake to the center of the screened interval.
   Avoid dropping the pump or allowing it to contact the bottom of
   the well.
2. Start the pump at the lowest speed setting and slowly increase until
   discharge begins. Target a flow rate of 0.1--0.5 L/min
   [@puls_barcelona1996; @astm_d6771].
3. Check the water level. Drawdown must not exceed 10 cm. If drawdown
   exceeds 10 cm, reduce the pumping rate.
4. Route discharge through the flow-through cell for continuous
   monitoring.
5. Record field parameters and cumulative purge volume on the purge log
   at 3--5 minute intervals.
6. Continue purging until field parameters have stabilized
   [@puls_barcelona1996]:

| Parameter              | Stabilization Criterion                       |
|:-----------------------|:----------------------------------------------|
| pH                     | ±0.1 units over three consecutive readings    |
| Temperature            | ±0.2 °C over three consecutive readings       |
| Specific conductance   | ±3% over three consecutive readings           |
| Dissolved oxygen       | ±0.3 mg/L over three consecutive readings     |
| ORP                    | ±10 mV over three consecutive readings        |
| Turbidity              | ±10% over three readings (or < 10 NTU)        |

7. Once all parameters are stable, proceed immediately to sample
   collection. Do not turn off the pump between purging and sampling.

::: {.callout-important}
### If the Well Purges Dry

If the well dewaters before stabilization, stop pumping and allow the
well to recover. Sample as soon as adequate volume has recovered.
Record the dewatering event and recovery time on the purge log. Note
that samples from wells purged to dryness may not be representative.
:::

### Sample Collection

1. Disconnect the flow-through cell from the discharge line. Collect
   samples directly from the pump tubing [@usepa_sesd301].
2. Maintain the same low flow rate used during purging.
3. Collect samples in this order to minimize bias:
   a. VOCs (if applicable) -- 40 mL glass vials, zero headspace
   b. Dissolved gases (if applicable)
   c. Total metals and other unfiltered analytes
   d. Filtered (dissolved) analytes -- attach a 0.45 µm in-line filter
   e. General chemistry (pH, conductivity, alkalinity, nutrients)
   f. Bacteria (use sterile bottles)
4. Fill bottles slowly to minimize aeration and turbulence.
5. Cap immediately, label, and place in ice.

### Post-Sampling Procedures

1. Measure and record the final depth to water.
2. Measure the total well depth.
3. Remove the pump and tubing. Replace the well cap and lock.
4. Containerize all purge water per the site waste management plan.
5. Decontaminate non-dedicated equipment and collect an equipment blank.
6. Complete the chain of custody form.

### Decontamination Between Wells

1. Flush the pump and tubing with ≥ 1 L of laboratory-grade detergent
   solution (Alconox or equivalent).
2. Flush with ≥ 3 L of deionized water.
3. Change nitrile gloves between wells.
4. Collect one equipment blank per sampling event [@apha2012].


## Sample Preservation and Holding Times

Follow preservation requirements specified by your analytical laboratory
[@apha2012]. Common groundwater analytes:

| Analyte              | Container          | Preservative           | Holding Time    |
|:---------------------|:-------------------|:-----------------------|:----------------|
| pH                   | Poly, 250 mL       | None; measure in field | 15 minutes      |
| Specific conductance | Poly, 250 mL       | Refrigerate 4 °C       | 28 days         |
| Alkalinity           | Poly, 250 mL       | Refrigerate 4 °C       | 14 days         |
| Nitrate + nitrite    | Poly, 250 mL       | H~2~SO~4~ to pH < 2; 4 °C | 28 days    |
| Total metals         | Poly, 500 mL       | HNO~3~ to pH < 2; 4 °C | 6 months       |
| Dissolved metals     | Poly, 500 mL       | Filter 0.45 µm; HNO~3~ to pH < 2; 4 °C | 6 months |
| VOCs                 | Glass, 40 mL (×3)  | HCl to pH < 2; 4 °C   | 14 days         |


## Quality Control

- **Field blank:** One per event; deionized water at the well site
  [@apha2012].
- **Equipment blank:** One per event from the final deionized rinse.
- **Field duplicates:** One per 10 wells sampled.
- **Trip blanks (VOCs only):** One per cooler.

## Training Record

Before sampling groundwater monitoring wells independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd), and
   [SOP-F300](SOP-F300-surface-water-sampling.qmd) in full
2. Review well construction logs for the wells to be sampled
3. Demonstrate proper water level measurement technique
4. Observe a trained operator complete a full low-flow purge and
   sample collection at one well
5. Perform a supervised purge and sampling event achieving
   stabilization within the criteria in §7.3
6. Demonstrate proper decontamination and chain of custody procedures
7. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
